Roasted Corn for Papa Zaka

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 4-6Prep 10 minCook 20-30 min

Roasted corn is a humble yet deeply significant dish for the Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa in Haitian Vodou. It symbolizes the bounty of the earth and the hard work of the farmer, serving as both a nourishing food for the community and a respectful offering to Papa Zaka, who presides over agriculture and harvest. This simple preparation honors the essence of the harvest.

Ingredients

  • 6 ears fresh corn on the cob, husked and silk removed
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) vegetable oil or olive oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) sea salt, or to taste
  • Optional: a pinch of black pepper

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Place the husked corn ears on a baking sheet.
  3. Drizzle the corn with vegetable oil, ensuring each ear is lightly coated. You can use your hands or a brush to spread the oil evenly.
  4. Sprinkle the corn evenly with sea salt and, if desired, a pinch of black pepper.
  5. Roast in the preheated oven for 20-30 minutes, turning the ears every 10 minutes, until the kernels are tender and slightly charred in spots.
  6. Remove from oven and serve hot.

Tips

  • For an even more rustic flavor, you can grill the corn directly over medium heat for 10-15 minutes, turning frequently, until tender and lightly charred.
  • A squeeze of lime juice after roasting can add a bright, fresh note that complements the sweetness of the corn.
  • If fresh corn is unavailable, frozen corn on the cob can be used; thaw completely before roasting.
